info.description:
The Uniqode API is organized around REST. Our API has predictable resource-oriented URLs, accepts form-encoded request bodies, returns JSON-encoded responses, and uses standard HTTP response codes, authentication, and verbs.

Authentication

The Uniqode API uses API key to authenticate requests.

Your API key carry many privileges, so be sure to keep them secure! Do not share your secret API keys in publicly accessible areas such as GitHub, client-side code, and so forth.

All API requests must be made over HTTPS. Calls made over plain HTTP will fail. API requests without authentication will also fail.

You can find your API key by using the following steps.

  1. Login to the Uniqode dashboard.

  2. Go to your 'API' section from the sidebar.

  3. Copy the API key value.

  4. Set a plain text header named Authorization with the contents of the header being Token XXX where XXX is your API Key.

Example header

curl -X "GET" "https://api.uniqode.com/api/2.0/qrcodes/" -H "Authorization: Token Your.API.Key-HERE" -H "Content-Type: application/json"

request.description:
Create a Geo Location QR Code

POST /api/2.0/qrcodes/

Creates a dynamic (qr_type: 2) QR Code whose scan destination is resolved by the scanning device's country.

Top-level request fields

Field Type Required Notes
name string yes QR Code display name
organization integer yes (or inferred from token) Org that owns the QR Code
qr_type integer yes 2 = Dynamic. Geo Location requires Dynamic — the campaign field is dropped server-side for Static (1) QR Codes
folder integer or null no Target folder id
metadata object no Free-form org metadata
campaign object yes for dynamic QR See campaign fields below

campaign object fields

Field Type Required Notes
content_type integer yes 22 = Geo Location
geo_location_content object yes, non-empty, when content_type = 22 See below

geo_location_content object

Field Type Required Notes
location_content object { [ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code]: { url, country } } yes Keys must be uppercase ISO alpha-2 country codes (US, IN, GB, …) — matched at scan-time against the CDN's CloudFront-Viewer-Country header, falling back to IP geolocation
location_content[code].url string (URL) yes for the entry referenced by default; recommended for all entries Destination URL for that country. No server-side URL-format validation beyond requiring a non-empty value for the default entry — the Angular dashboard additionally regex-validates every URL and auto-prefixes https:// if a scheme is missing
location_content[code].country string no Display label only (e.g. "United States") — never read by validation or the redirect resolver, purely cosmetic
default string yes Must be a key present in location_content. Used as the fallback destination when the scanner's country isn't in location_content (unless restrict_default_redirect is true)
restrict_default_redirect boolean no (default false) Must be a literal JSON boolean (true/false) — a string value fails validation. When true, scans from a country not listed in location_content show a "not available in your country" error page instead of falling back to default

Country limit

The number of keys in location_content is capped by the Account's plan. Exceeding it returns 426 Upgrade Required (see Error Codes).

Response (201 Created)

{
  "id": 987654,
  "name": "GEO_LOCATION Example QR",
  "qr_type": 2,
  "state": "A",
  "url": "https://uniqo.de/abc123",
  "domain": 2,
  "folder": null,
  "metadata": {},
  "attributes": { "...": "..." },
  "campaign": {
    "content_type": 22,
    "campaign_active": true,
    "timezone": "Asia/Calcutta",
    "age_gate": null,
    "geo_location_content": {
      "location_content": {
        "US": { "url": "https://example.com", "country": "United States" },
        "IN": { "url": "https://example.com/in", "country": "India" },
        "GB": { "url": "https://example.com/uk", "country": "United Kingdom" }
      },
      "default": "US",
      "restrict_default_redirect": false
    }
  },
  "organization": 26724,
  "created": "2026-08-04T10:30:00Z",
  "updated": "2026-08-04T10:30:00Z"
}

Error responses

Status Cause Body
400 content_type: 22 sent without a non-empty geo_location_content {"campaign": ["You must pass a non-empty geo_location_content field when content_type is geo_location_content"]}
400 default missing {"campaign": {"geo_location_content": ["default language has to be specified for geo_location campaigns"]}}
400 default key not present in location_content {"campaign": {"geo_location_content": ["default language key not present in location_content"]}}
400 No url on the default country's entry {"campaign": {"geo_location_content": ["No URL in default content for geo_location_content"]}}
400 restrict_default_redirect not a boolean {"campaign": {"geo_location_content": ["restrict_default_redirect value should be a boolean always"]}}
426 Number of countries in location_content exceeds the org's plan limit (create only) {"detail": "Geo Location Content limit of current plan exceeded. Please upgrade to a higher plan."}
426 Dynamic QR Code count limit reached for the org's plan {"detail": "Dynamic QR code limit ..."}
409 Integrity error (e.g. duplicate slug) {"detail": "IntegrityError - Invalid input"}

BulkQRCode objects allow you to perform actions on create a collection of QR Codes in a single request. You can create a QR Code collection, retrieve or update individual QR Code collections as well as a list of all your QR Code collections.

The behaviour of BulkQRCode objects is currently restricted to static QR Codes only.

BulkQRCode objects support all values for attributes supported by the QRCode object. You can also pass individual attribute data in the CSV file used to create the Bulk QR Code collection, this allows you to create QR Codes with different designs in a single collection.

Media objects allow you to upload files such as images, documents into Uniqode and use them with campaigns through Beaconstac products. You can create a Media object, retrieve or update individual Media objects as well as a list of all the Media objects in your account.

Uniqode uses the S3 service from Amazon Web Services to store files. In order to upload a file to Uniqode, use the Media API to first create a Media object, which returns the policy details and necessary information required to upload a file to Uniqode. Once upload is completed, update the Media object with the appropriate information so that you can reference the object to access the files in the future.
